info.title: seren-passwords
info.description: End-to-end-encrypted credential vault. The server stores only ciphertext; clients perform encryption and decryption. Every protected route requires gateway-injected identity headers (X-Seren-User-Id, X-Seren-Organization-Id, optional X-Seren-Agent-Identity-Id).

put.summary: Set up the caller's account in the org vault database.
put.description:
The first call creates the user's identity, seeds the account_secrets row,
and provisions the default Personal vault in one transaction. If the
account is already initialized, the endpoint returns the existing setup
state and does not overwrite any key material.

400.description: Malformed setup body

403.description: Agents may not set up user accounts

409.description: Partial existing state; refusing to overwrite

post.summary:
Complete account recovery: replace account_secrets with a freshly wrapped
blob and rotate the recovery key.
post.description:
Verifies the recovery proof signature over the open challenge plus the
new KEM public key, and rejects completions that reuse the existing
recovery_key_wrap or recovery_kdf_params (so a leaked recovery sheet must
also be retired).

400.description: Recovery blob attempted to rotate identity keys, or recovery key was not rotated

403.description: Agents may not complete account recovery

404.description: No active identity or matching recovery request

409.description: Recovery request was consumed or expired during verification

post.summary: Open an account recovery request and receive a random challenge.
post.description:
The client signs the challenge plus the new KEM public key in
`/account/recovery/complete` to prove possession of the existing account
signing key (recovered using the recovery key).

403.description: Agents may not initiate account recovery

404.description: No active identity for this user

get.summary: Fetch the caller's opaque account_secrets blob.
get.description:
Returns the wrapped account, KEM, signing, and recovery keys; the server
stores them only as ciphertext. A 404 here means the user has not yet
set up an account in this org's vault database - the client should call
`PUT /account` to do that.

404.description: Account not initialized in this org yet

400.description: Malformed body or timestamp outside the freshness window

403.description: Agents may not update account secrets

404.description: Account is not initialized in this org

409.description: Partial existing state, or a stale/replayed update proof

get.summary:
List item summaries in a vault, optionally filtered by lifecycle state,

parameters.name: title_blind_index
parameters.description: Optional base64-encoded blind-index for exact title lookup.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
Lifecycle state to list. Defaults to active. `trashed` returns
items in the trash (DELETE'd but not yet hard-deleted); `archived`
returns archived items (the existing `archived_at` lifecycle).

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description:
RFC3339 timestamp. When set, only items with `updated_at`
strictly greater than this point appear in the result. Delta-sync
callers should pass the most recent `updated_at` they have
already ingested; the boundary row is excluded so polling does
not re-deliver it.

AccountSecretsUpdateRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /account/secrets`.

Rotates the existing account_secrets blob under a freshly-derived
master-password key or recovery key. The update proof binds the new blob
digest to the existing account signing key so a stolen Seren session cannot
overwrite the user's encrypted private material.

issued_at.description:
RFC3339 timestamp the client signed. Server rejects outside the
UPDATE_PROOF_WINDOW to bound replay.

update_proof_signature.description:
Ed25519 signature over the canonical proof bytes (user_id, issued_at,
blob_digest) produced by the existing account signing key.

AccountSetupRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /account`.

First-time setup creates the user's E2EE identity, stores the opaque
account_secrets blob, and provisions the default Personal vault in one
transaction. The server receives only public identity material, ciphertext
wraps, and the client's signed vault-membership grant.

display_name.description: Display name for the new user identity.

personal_vault_granted_signature.description:
Ed25519 signature granting the new identity admin membership in the
Personal vault.

personal_vault_id.description:
Client-generated Personal vault id. The id is bound into the
encrypted vault label AAD, so the client must know it before setup.

personal_vault_wrapped_key.description: Wrapped Personal vault key under the new identity's KEM public key.

identity.description: The caller's active user identity in this org.

AgentSummary.description:
An owned agent identity plus the vaults it currently has access to.
Returned by `GET /identities/agents` to power `seren passwords agent list`.

AgentVaultGrant.description:
A single vault grant held by an agent identity, returned by
`GET /identities/agents`. Carries only public metadata: the vault id, the
access level, and when the grant was made. No wrapped key material.

ApproveContext.description:
Material an approver needs to construct the `one_shot_wrapped_key`
for `POST /approvals/{id}/approve`. The wrap is built client-side:
the approver seals the per-item content key (item targets) or the
vault key (vault targets) under the requester's identity KEM public
key.

For item targets the server returns the item's `content_key_wrap` so
the approver can unwrap the content key with their vault key and
then re-seal it for the requester. For vault targets only the
requester KEM pub and vault id are returned, since the approver
already has the vault key in memory.

approver_wrapped_vault_key.description:
Base64. The approver's own wrapped vault key for the target
vault, so the approver can unwrap the vault key on the client
without a second round-trip.

content_key_wrap.description: Base64. Only set for item-kind approvals.

item_id.description:
Only set for item-kind approvals. The item id is required by the
approver because the per-item content-key wrap AAD binds to it;
returning it here lets the client unwrap without consulting any
separately-loaded approval listing.

requester_kem_public_key.description:
Base64. The requester identity's KEM public key. The approver
uses this to KEM-seal the wrapped material.

blob.description:
Base64-encoded encrypted blob bytes the client must decrypt with the
unwrapped attachment key and the (item_id, attachment_id) AAD.

BatchEntryResult.description:
One entry in a batch resolve response, position-aligned with the
corresponding request. `Ok` carries the wrapped material; the other
variants surface the error so an investigator and the calling runtime
can see exactly which URIs failed and why without parsing free-form
strings.

recipient_email.description: Required when the share was restricted to an email address.

CreateAgentIdentityRequest.description: Body for creating an agent identity.

issued_at.description:
Unix seconds when the owner signed this request. The server bounds the
allowed skew so a captured signature cannot be replayed indefinitely.

nonce.description: Single-use nonce bound into the signed canonical bytes.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature by the owning user over the canonical request bytes.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to keep the request pending; defaults to 300.

attachment_id.description:
Client-generated attachment id used in the AEAD associated data for
the blob, metadata, and wrapped attachment key.

blob.description:
The encrypted attachment blob (XChaCha20-Poly1305 envelope under the
per-attachment content key, AAD-bound to (item_id, attachment_id)).

content_type_ciphertext.description: AEAD envelope of the content-type under the vault key.

filename_ciphertext.description: AEAD envelope of the filename under the vault key.

wrapped_content_key.description: The per-attachment content key wrapped under the vault key.

CreateHostedAgentIdentityRequest.description:
Body for creating a hosted agent identity whose private keys are generated
server-side and stored only as KMS-wrapped envelopes.

issued_at.description: Unix seconds when the owner signed this hosted identity request.

nonce.description: Single-use nonce bound into the signed canonical bytes.

signature.description:
Ed25519 signature by the owning user over the canonical hosted identity
request bytes.

expires_in_hours.description:
Omit for the default 14 days, send null for no expiration, or
send hours clamped to 1 hour through 1 year.

content_key_wrap.description:
Per-item content key sealed under the vault key (see
crypto::protocol::item::wrap_item_content_key). The body ciphertext
is sealed under that content key, never directly under the vault
key; the server enforces presence with a NOT NULL column.

wrapping_key_version.description:
The `vault_key_version` the client believed it was sealing under
when it produced these ciphertexts. The server rejects the write
with 409 Conflict if it does not match the vault's current
version, so a client that raced a key rotation must re-fetch its
wrapped vault key and re-encrypt before retrying.

expires_in_hours.description:
Omit for the default 14 days, send null for no expiration, or
send hours clamped to 1 hour through 1 year.

recipient_email.description:
Plaintext email is used transiently for invite delivery and claim
authorization. It is never persisted.

DataResponseJsonValue.description:
`data: serde_json::Value` envelopes used by endpoints that return ad-hoc
JSON payloads (e.g. `{ "revoked": true }`, `{ "completed": true }`).
The schema is intentionally open: utoipa renders `Value` as the generic
JSON Object type.

oneOf.description:
Present when a recorded contribution can be resubmitted to finish an
incomplete grant application.

DelegationRecordedContribution.description:
The participant's own recorded contribution, returned only while its grant
application is incomplete. A resume must resubmit this material unchanged:
vault-key wraps are non-deterministic sealed boxes, so a rebuilt wrap can
never reproduce the recorded scope hash and the server refuses it as a
replacement of recorded key material.

attachments.description:
Re-encrypted attachments for the duplicated item. Each source
attachment must be represented exactly once because attachment blobs are
AAD-bound to both item id and attachment id.

content_key_wrap.description:
Per-item content key sealed under the destination vault key and bound
to the new item id.

item_id.description:
New item id. Item ciphertext AAD is item-id-bound, so clients must
encrypt the duplicate payload for this id.

target_vault_id.description: Destination vault. Defaults to the source vault.

wrapping_key_version.description:
Destination vault key version used for every vault-key-scoped
ciphertext in this payload.

invitation_token.description: One-shot token. Treat as a secret; never echoed by other endpoints.

trashed_at.description:
Set when the item is in the trash. Distinct from `archived_at`.
A second DELETE on a trashed item hard-deletes the row entirely.

vault_key_version.description:
Vault key version under which this row's ciphertexts were sealed.
Clients echo it back on PATCH via `wrapping_key_version` to guard
against rotation races; the server rejects with 409 on mismatch.

share_token.description: Signed routing token. Send it only through the intended invite path.

attachments.description:
Re-wrapped attachment metadata for the moved item. Blob ciphertext is
unchanged on move because item id and attachment ids stay stable.

content_key_wrap.description:
Per-item content key re-wrapped under the destination vault key and
still bound to the existing item id.

wrapping_key_version.description:
Destination vault key version used for every vault-key-scoped
ciphertext in this payload.

new_account_secrets.description:
New AccountSecrets blob the client built by re-wrapping the existing
account_key under a new master-password-derived key. Recovery does not
rotate identity public keys; clients must keep both public halves equal
to the existing active identity.

challenge.description: 32 random bytes base64-encoded. Bind this into the proof on /complete.

RecoveryNewAccountSecrets.description:
New account-secrets blob submitted alongside a recovery completion.

Recovery rewraps the existing account key under a new master-password-
derived key and rotates the recovery key; the identity public keys are
re-asserted (server checks they did not change) but no personal-vault or
display-name material is involved. This is a strict subset of the
first-time setup request body in `routes::account`.

issued_at.description:
RFC3339 timestamp the client signed. Server rejects if outside the
SIGNATURE_WINDOW around its own clock.

nonce.description: Single-use nonce bound into the signature and consumed by the service.

request_signature.description:
Ed25519 signature over the canonical request, produced by the caller's
identity signing key (the user's or the agent's). Wire encoding from
the crypto crate (versioned).

content_ciphertext.description: Base64 - the item body, sealed under the per-item content key.

content_key_wrap.description:
Base64 - the per-item content key sealed under the vault key.
Agent unwraps the vault key first, then opens this to recover the
content key, then opens `content_ciphertext` with it.

wrapped_vault_key.description: Base64 - the caller's wrapped vault key.

RotationItemDto.description:
Per-item payload for a rotation commit. The body ciphertext is sealed
under the per-item content key and does not change across rotations;
the client only re-wraps the content key under the new vault key.
The title, tags, and blind index keying material are still vault-key
scoped, so those are re-derived and shipped alongside.

content_key_wrap.description: Per-item content key re-wrapped under the new vault key.

SharedItemRecord.description:
The owner item as seen by a live-share recipient. Omits `content_key_wrap`
(sealed under the owner's vault key, so opaque and useless to the recipient,
who opens the body via `recipient_wrapped_item_key`) and `title_blind_index`
(an owner-scoped keyed index over the plaintext title).

foreign_memberships.description:
Active cross-organization memberships for local vaults the caller can
see. Used by rotation to re-wrap foreign recipients without requiring
local identity rows.

identities.description:
Active identities visible to this caller (org-scoped). Useful for
the desktop client to populate the "share with" picker without a
separate `/identities` fetch.

item_overviews.description:
Active item overviews across every vault returned above. Bodies
are not included (the client fetches `/items/{id}` on demand).

memberships.description:
Active memberships across every vault returned above. The client
uses these to render the per-vault member list without one
`/vaults/{v}/memberships` round-trip per vault.

server_time.description:
RFC3339 UTC timestamp from the server's clock. Clients use this to
calibrate their resolve-signature `issued_at` window.

vaults.description:
Vaults the caller is a member of, each with the caller's wrapped
vault key inlined so the client can immediately decrypt content.

content_key_wrap.description:
Per-item content key sealed under the vault key. Required on every
update; the body ciphertext is sealed under it.

wrapping_key_version.description:
The `vault_key_version` the client believed it was sealing under.
See `CreateItemRequest::wrapping_key_version`.

VaultPatchRequest.description:
Documentary schema for `PATCH /vaults/{vault_id}`. The runtime body
is a free-form JSON object; at least one of `name_ciphertext` or `description_ciphertext`
must be present.

`description_ciphertext` uses a double `Option` so the route can distinguish
the three caller intents the column allows: omit the field to leave
it alone, send `null` to clear it, or send ciphertext to set it.
`name_ciphertext` is `NOT NULL` in the schema so the single-`Option` shape
covers its two intents (omit vs set).

vault_key_version.description:
Monotone counter incremented on every completed key rotation.
Clients echo it on item writes via `wrapping_key_version` to
guard against rotation races.

wrapped_vault_key.description: Present when listing or fetching the vault on behalf of a member.

bearer_auth.description: Seren publisher gateway authentication. The gateway validates the caller and injects X-Seren-User-Id, X-Seren-Organization-Id, and optional X-Seren-Agent-Identity-Id before requests reach this service.
